Subject: Clarify: ephemeral session logs / deletion commitments

Hi Jasmine / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team had a follow-up specifically about short-lived runtime logs for inference sessions. Two asks: 1) can you confirm whether session-level logs (request/response payloads used for model routing decisions) are retained by default, and if so for how long? 2) For the VPC/private deployment we plan to use, can Redwood commit to a 14-day maximum retention window for those ephemeral logs and provide evidence we can include in our SIG questionnaire?

We attached a short spreadsheet with the fields they expect (medivantage-ephemeral-ask.xlsx). If a shorter retention window is possible only with specific config/flags or with an add-on (e.g., dedicated-only), please call that out. Also let us know any limitations around legal hold / eDiscovery requests — our legal team will want to understand exception handling.

Can we get a first-pass reply by EOD Friday?

Appreciate it,
Rachel
Senior InfoSec Analyst
MediVantage

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: ephemeral session logs / deletion commitments

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Short answers up front: default hosted retention for full request/response logs is 90 days; for Dedicated/Private there are configurable retention controls and we can support a 14-day window in most Private deployments with the right config and an operational runbook. A few caveats below (legal hold, metrics/audit trails).

Details:
- What we mean by "session-level logs": request metadata, routing decisions, and (optionally) non-persistent request payloads. We do not persist model KV caches as logs — those are in-memory and not written to disk in normal operation.
- Hosted (Redwood API): persistent debug logs and request payloads are retained 90 days by default for troubleshooting and quality monitoring. Shortening to 14 days is possible only for dedicated/private where customer controls retention settings.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): we can configure the pipeline to expire session logs after 14 days; the config is documented and includes a retention TTL on the logging backend (Elasticsearch/managed object store). We will ship sample config and the manual steps required to enforce deletion.
- Legal hold / eDiscovery: deletions are soft-delete with deletion markers for a short grace window to support recovery. For customers that require guaranteed immutability for legal hold, we have a documented escalation path to pause purge jobs; this is an operational exception and requires signed change control (we'll include the process in the evidence package).

Next steps I propose:
1) Neha and I will prepare a small evidence bundle (SOC 2 template artifacts + sample retention config + deletion runbook) and return it to you by Tue 23 Mar EOD.
2) If MediVantage needs a firm contractual SLA (14-day retention guaranteed), we should record that as a customer-specific exception in the contract with an associated security compensating control. Please indicate if legal wants that in the MSA.
3) Optional: schedule a 30-min technical call with our infra engineer to walk the config.

Looping in Neha to own the artifacts and Laura to help with any contract language.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu

Rachel — quick note from the contracts side. If MediVantage requires a contractual commitment to 14-day retention for specific log types we will need:
- A short addendum listing the exact artifacts covered (e.g., session request/response payloads, routing logs)
- Acceptance criteria for "deletion" (soft-delete vs physical purge)
- Agreed SLA for exceptions (who to notify, timeline to suspend purge)
- A compensating control if Redwood cannot guarantee physical immutability (e.g., compressed/archived exports for legal hold under customer direction)

If you can confirm the exact artifact list we can draft language to attach to the MSA. Happy to join a call with your legal team.

Hi all — attaching the evidence bundle we discussed and a short sample log extract showing TTL metadata (soc2-logs-evidence-sample.txt). Key points:
- For Private/VPC deployments we expose a retention TTL per-log-index and a configurable purge job that runs with a 24h window.
- To enforce 14 days we set TTL=14 and enable immediate purge after the 24h grace run; we document the orchestration steps in the runbook.
- Legal hold: toggling hold flips off the purge job; the toggle is audit-logged and requires two approvers (customer admin + Redwood security).

Links: SEC-412 in our tracker has the open implementation ticket. I've included the Drive link to the runbook in the related_links field.

Deliverables in this bundle:
- retention-config-snippet (json)
- purge-runbook (markdown)
- sample-ttl-log-entry (soc2-logs-evidence-sample.txt)

If MediVantage wants us to attach the addendum language to the MSA, Laura - please propose a short clause and we will validate operational feasibility.

Thanks — received the bundle and reviewed. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we ask legal to draft the addendum:
1) Does the TTL-based purge remove attachments stored in logs (for example, base64 snippets) or only metadata?
2) For the "two-approver" legal hold flow, can MediVantage be configured as the second approver or is the second approver always an internal Redwood role?
3) If we request occasional exports to preserve data for litigation, is there an automated export endpoint or is that handled manually by Redwood ops?

If you can answer these 3 items we can decide whether to request the contractual addendum or rely on the operational runbook.

Best,
Rachel

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Myers <rachel.myers@medivantage.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-27T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: ephemeral session logs / deletion commitments

Rachel — answers inline below.

1) TTL purge scope: the purge job removes any stored payloads that are indexed in the logging backend, including base64-encoded attachments that were persisted into the same log index. If attachments were stored externally (e.g., object storage with separate lifecycle rules), those are subject to the object-store TTL and may require a separate purge. We'll include a mapping table in the runbook showing where each artifact type lives.

2) Two-approver hold: we can support MediVantage as one approver (customer admin). The second approver can be an assigned Redwood security contact. We record both approvals in the audit log with timestamps and admin IDs.

3) Exports: we provide an operator-driven export endpoint for ad-hoc preservation; exports are initiated by a Redwood ops runbook and produce a compressed archive to a customer-controlled S3 location (or to our secure transfer link). Automated scheduled exports are available as an add-on; if you need that we can price it.

Action items:
- I'll attach the runbook and sample retention config to this thread (sent separately to your Drive link).
- Laura will draft a short addendum clause; Rachel, please confirm whether you want the clause in the MSA or if operational controls suffice for now.
- If you want a walkthrough, pick a slot next week (I can do Tue/Wed afternoon PT).

Thanks — happy to keep iterating.
